claims.title: Spanish reach the isthmus
claims.summary: Rodrigo de Bastidas and then Christopher Columbus explore the Caribbean coast of the isthmus, opening the region to Spanish colonisation.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Panama: The isthmus that joined two oceans and two Americas, from Balboa's South Sea to the canal returned.", terralore.co/country/PAN/chronicle#ev-1501-spanish-reach-the-isthmus, claim TL:PAN:event:1501:spanish-reach-the-isthmus, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Balboa sights the Pacific
claims.summary: Vasco Nunez de Balboa crosses the isthmus and becomes the first European to see the Pacific Ocean from the Americas, claiming it for Castile.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Panama: The isthmus that joined two oceans and two Americas, from Balboa's South Sea to the canal returned.", terralore.co/country/PAN/chronicle#ev-1513-balboa-sights-the-pacific, claim TL:PAN:event:1513:balboa-sights-the-pacific, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Balboa executed
claims.summary: Accused of treason by the governor Pedrarias Davila, Balboa is beheaded, the same year a new Pacific-coast city is founded.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Panama: The isthmus that joined two oceans and two Americas, from Balboa's South Sea to the canal returned.", terralore.co/country/PAN/chronicle#ev-1519-balboa-executed, claim TL:PAN:event:1519:balboa-executed, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Founding of Panama Viejo
claims.summary: Pedrarias Davila founds Panama on the Pacific coast, the oldest European city on the Pacific shore of the Americas and a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

sources.label: El Sitio Arqueológico de Panamá Viejo

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Panama: The isthmus that joined two oceans and two Americas, from Balboa's South Sea to the canal returned.", terralore.co/country/PAN/chronicle#ev-1519-founding-of-panama-viejo, claim TL:PAN:event:1519:founding-of-panama-viejo, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Trade shifts to Portobelo
claims.summary: Spain moves its Caribbean treasure port to Portobelo, whose fairs and fortifications anchor the trans-isthmus gold and silver route.

sources.label: Fortifications on the Caribbean Side of Panama: Portobelo-San Lorenzo

claims.title: Henry Morgan sacks Panama
claims.summary: The buccaneer Henry Morgan crosses the isthmus and takes Panama Viejo, which burns to the ground; the city is refounded on a new site in 1673.

sources.label: El Sitio Arqueológico de Panamá Viejo

claims.title: Independence from Spain and union
claims.summary: Panama declares independence from Spain and voluntarily joins Gran Colombia, remaining tied to Colombia after Gran Colombia dissolves.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Panama: The isthmus that joined two oceans and two Americas, from Balboa's South Sea to the canal returned.", terralore.co/country/PAN/chronicle#ev-1821-independence-from-spain-and-union, claim TL:PAN:event:1821:independence-from-spain-and-union, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Panama Railroad completed
claims.summary: Spurred by the California Gold Rush, a U.S. company completes the trans-isthmus railroad, the shortest route between the oceans.

claims.title: French canal attempt fails
claims.summary: Ferdinand de Lesseps's company begins a sea-level canal but is defeated by disease and cost, collapsing in financial scandal.

claims.summary: With U.S. backing, Panama declares independence from Colombia and is swiftly recognised by the United States.

claims.summary: The treaty grants the United States a Canal Zone across the isthmus in perpetuity and guarantees Panama's independence.

sources.publisher: U.S. Department of State, Office of the Historian

claims.title: Panama Canal opens
claims.summary: After a decade of U.S. construction, the lock canal opens to traffic, joining the Atlantic and Pacific oceans.

claims.summary: Clashes over flying the Panamanian flag in the Canal Zone leave roughly two dozen Panamanians and several Americans dead, hardening demands to revise the 1903 treaty.

claims.summary: A military coup brings General Omar Torrijos to power; his government makes recovery of the canal its central aim.

claims.summary: Torrijos and President Carter sign treaties abolishing the Canal Zone and committing to transfer the canal to Panama by the end of 1999.
